public_payload.normalized_proposition: Oracle is staking its future on Stargate projects that will take years to turn a profit even if OpenAI pays on time.
conditions: even if OpenAI pays on time

statement.excerpt: I should also be clear that Oracle is mortgaging its entire fucking future on projects like Stargate Abilene, incurring billions of dollars of costs up front for a business that will take years to turn a profit even if OpenAI makes every single payment in a timely manner.

from_speaker: incurring billions of dollars of costs up front
will take years to turn a profit
even if OpenAI makes every single payment in a timely manner
our_interpretation: The plain reading concerns Oracle's Stargate projects, not Oracle's consolidated profitability.
I read 'years' as multiple years after commercial operations begin. The speaker supplies neither a calendar deadline nor a precise starting point.
I read profit as project earnings after attributable costs. Recovering the original investment is a different measure and must be reported separately.
'Even if' describes a best-case payment scenario rather than an antecedent that must occur before the forecast applies. Losses caused by missed payments would not establish the stronger claim.
'Mortgaging its entire future' expresses the scale of the alleged exposure; it supplies no separate measurable threshold.
criteria.support_condition: Project accounts establish that first profitability took multiple years despite timely customer payments, with attributable upfront costs documented.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Project accounts establish profitability before two years of commercial operations under timely payments, on a measure that includes the relevant project costs.
